extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and evaluators of LLM creative writing; computational linguists and creative-writing assessment researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of generated short creative narratives by LLMs (and human writers) using a task-specific rubric and human judgments to compare dimensions such as readability, style imitation, humor, and originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Readability (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses clarity and ease of reading; listed as a more technical aspect where LLMs tended to perform well. No further sub-rules given on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key narrative elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Key narrative elements (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates presence and handling of essential narrative components (e.g., exposition, conflict, resolution). The rubric was adapted from prior craft-based rubrics for creative writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural elements (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges story organization and structural coherence (e.g., paragraphing, pacing). Identified as a technical aspect where many LLMs outperformed humans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot logic (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures logical consistency of the plot and causal connections between events; important for credibility of the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity / originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Creativity (originality) (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses novelty and originality of ideas and expression. The paper highlights that this was the only item where human writers outperformed all LLMs, indicating humans retain an edge on originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation of John Kennedy Toole style
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporation of John Kennedy Toole style (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates how well the story mimics or evokes the specific target author's style (register, voice, lexical and syntactic choices). The task explicitly requested writing 'in the style of John Kennedy Toole.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Epic genre inhabitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Epic genre (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses understanding and habitation of epic-genre conventions (tone, scope, elevated language). LLMs performed strongly on this dimension in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description and credibility of combat
rubrics_metrics.description: Description and credibility of combat (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically measures how well the combat scene is described and whether the combat details are credible and vivid given the task's single-combat scenario.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Main characters (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates characterization of protagonists/antagonists (development, distinctness, consistency). In this task, includes handling of the pre-defined character Ignatius J. Reilly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dark humor / Humor
rubrics_metrics.description: Dark humor (humor) (one of the ten rubric items; rated on a 1–10 scale).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses presence and effectiveness of humor (especially dark or author-specific humor). The study notes humor was the most difficult item overall (mean ≈ 3.4) and only a few models matched human levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale: 1–10 per item
rubrics_metrics.description: Each rubric dimension is scored on a 1–10 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual item scores are averaged to compute overall ratings. The rubric adapted prior craft-based assessment work and applied the 1–10 scale across ten dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall rating (average across rubric items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall rating computed as the average of all rubric item scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for model ranking and comparisons; statistical tests on overall rating were reported (and finer-grained tests on individual-item datapoints were also performed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation methodology / human-judgment protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Human-based evaluation protocol and reliability controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details: 10 raters conducted evaluations; each rater was given 13 stories (one human and one per each of 12 LLMs) in blind conditions (raters did not know which was which). Models were prompted 5 times each from a fresh state to capture output variability; 5 human writers produced comparable-length stories. Agreement measured (weighted Cohen’s kappa = 0.48, moderate). These procedural choices are part of the study's reliability standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt / data-contamination avoidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Design prompts to minimize training data leakage and force creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study used a custom zero-shot prompt featuring an unlikely scenario ('Write an epic narration of a single combat between Ignatius J. Reilly and a pterodactyl, in the style of John Kennedy Toole') to avoid copying existing texts from training data. The paper notes this approach reduces contamination risk but becomes less reusable after publication (since the prompt and generated corpus can enter training data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length parity between human and model outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Human writers were asked to produce stories of similar length to LLM outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures length is not a confounding variable in evaluation; a procedural control used in the study to make human and model outputs comparable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple samples per model to account for randomness
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate multiple outputs per model (5 fresh-state prompts per model) to measure reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sampling multiple generations per model captures inherent randomness in LLM outputs and supports more robust comparison to humans.
